usage:
hergy - run a team of agents on top of herdr

Usage: hergy <command> [options]

Run a team
  up [definition]          Start a team
  down [team]              Stop a team, and close the workers it hired
  status [team]            Show how the members and workers are doing
  refresh <member>|--all   Restart a member; its conversation starts empty
  reprompt <member>|--all  Send the bootstrap prompt again; the conversation stays
  hire <name>              Add a worker

Team definitions
  new <definition>         Write a starter team definition
  ls                       List the team definitions
  show <definition>        Show the final team definition and where each value came from
  validate                 Check the settings files
  serve                    Open the web UI in a browser

Other
  cheat [--ai]             Show the cheatsheet
  version                  Show the version

Common options
  --dry                    Show what would happen, and do nothing
  --as <team>              Run the same team definition under another team name (up only)
  --team <team>            The team for refresh, reprompt and hire
  --global / --local       Use only the global or the project team definitions
  -C <dir>                 Use this directory as the project
  --lang en|ja             Language of the output (default en)
  --port <port>            The port hergy serve listens on (default 8787)

Options for hire
  --purpose <purpose> --task "<task>" [--profile <profile>] [--from <member>]

Where team definitions live
  Project                  .hergy/teams/<definition>/team.yaml
  Global                   ~/.config/hergy/teams/<definition>/team.yaml

Details of one command: hergy <command> --help
cheat.people:
hergy cheat

First time
  hergy new myteam  Write a starter team definition
  edit team.yaml    Write the members and the agents they run
  hergy up myteam   Start the team (--dry to only look)

Everyday commands
  Start a team                     hergy up [definition]
  Stop a team                      hergy down [team]
  See how the team is doing        hergy status [team]
  Restart a member                 hergy refresh <member>
  Send the bootstrap prompt again  hergy reprompt <member>
  Add a worker                     hergy hire <name> --purpose X --task "..." [--profile P]
  List the team definitions        hergy ls
  Look at a team definition        hergy show <definition>
  Check the settings               hergy validate
  Show the version                 hergy version
  Open the web UI                  hergy serve [--port <port>]

Web UI screens (hergy serve)
  home             /
  team list        /teams
  rules            /rules
  prompt diff      /diff
  raise a version  /bump
  team definition  /team
  running teams    /running
  figure           /figure

Where team definitions live
  Project  .hergy/teams/<definition>/team.yaml
  Global   ~/.config/hergy/teams/<definition>/team.yaml

Options of each command: hergy <command> --help. All commands: hergy --help. For an agent: hergy cheat --ai

herdr.guide_member:
- To a member: `herdr agent prompt <name> "<text>"`. Start the text with "%s".
- To the human: write in your own pane.
- For anything else: `herdr agent --help`.
- To add a teammate, use `hergy hire`, not `herdr agent start`: a teammate herdr starts directly is invisible to hergy's roster, `hergy down` and `hergy status`.
herdr.guide_worker:
- To a member: `herdr agent prompt <name> "<text>"`. Start the text with "%s".
- To the human: write in your own pane.
- For anything else: `herdr agent --help`.
- A worker adds no teammates: reach the others with `herdr agent prompt`, and ask the member that hired you if another worker is needed.
spawn.note:
## Spawning workers
When needed, you may spawn a worker for one of these purpose-to-profile pairs: %s
How to spawn: `%s`
The worker starts in another tab; its herdr name is "<team>-<worker>". It reports back to you (%s) when done. Worker names are lower-case ASCII and must not collide with the roster.

web.rules.panel.title: Edit a rule
web.rules.field.send_why: Send the reason in the prompt too (hergy counts the rule as one with a reason even when this is not ticked)
web.rules.field.note: The note (counted as neither a reason nor an origin)
web.rules.origin.refs: References (an issue number, a gy id, a URL; separated by commas)
web.rules.origin.refs.derived: The ids of the rules it came from (separated by commas)
web.rules.origin.what: An origin is the record of when a rule was written and what put it there. It is an incident, an instruction, or another rule it was derived from.
web.rules.origin.why: A rule whose origin is known can be judged later and dropped when it is no longer needed. A rule with no origin can be judged by nobody, so it stays and hardens.
web.rules.field.tests: The ids of the test scenarios (separated by commas)
web.rules.panel.preview.empty: The text of this rule is empty

web.bump.title: Raise a version
web.bump.lede: This screen lists the documents of the %s whose content moved since the last launch. Raising a document's version says the change is worth handing over. A document with no version is at 0, so raising it writes 1. The next `hergy up` then hands the change to the members that read the document.
web.bump.already: This document's version was raised after the last launch.
web.bump.global: This document is in the global layer: raising its version reaches every project that uses it.
web.bump.next: The next `hergy up %s` hands the change to the members that read the document.
web.bump.none: No document of this layer has moved since the last launch, so there is no version to raise.
web.bump.no_record: No team definition of this layer has been launched from this machine yet, so there is nothing to raise: this screen compares the files with what the last launch read. `hergy up <name>` boots a team and records the launch.
web.diff.title: Prompt diff
web.diff.lede: This screen shows one team definition of the %s at a time. For each member it lines up the prompt that was last handed over with the prompt the files build now, line by line.
web.diff.empty: No team definition of this layer can be read, so there is no prompt to compare.
web.diff.no_launch: This team definition has not been launched from this machine yet. `hergy up <name>` hands the prompts over and records the launch.
web.diff.member_never: %s: no launch has handed this member a prompt yet.
